brief.premise: A Harbor Commission safety inspector investigates the reported voluntary departure of a remote lighthouse keeper, reconstructing the night from log books, weather records, supply manifests, and radio logs.
brief.setting: Remote coastal lighthouse station on an exposed rock station with supply landing, keeper quarters, lamp gallery, maintenance workshop, and records office
brief.investigator_character: Harbor Commission safety inspector dispatched to verify keeper status and reconstruct the overnight timeline
brief.opening_situation: You arrive by rotor to find relief keeper Sarah Chen waiting on the landing. Assistant keeper Tom Reed claims head keeper Henry Walsh departed voluntarily at 0430, but the station records disagree.
initial_observable_facts: The landing shows storm debris and an unloaded personal trunk tagged for Henry Walsh.
The lamp is operating, but keeper handover was not completed.
Tom Reed has already logged a voluntary departure in the keeper's log.
Commission radio expects your reconstruction report by 1300.
brief.in_world_duration: one inspection day (approximately four in-world hours)
brief.location_scale: single remote lighthouse station with five primary locations
brief.content_boundaries: no graphic violence; no supernatural elements; workplace negligence and cover-up themes; death by accidental fall; no sexual content
required_themes: one perfect ending and several imperfect endings
brief.deadline_or_constraint: Commission report due at 1300; landing weather may close again
brief.author_notes: Codename: The Harbor Light Signal. Culprit NPC-TOM covered up keeper death during unauthorized lens repair. Emphasis on logs, weather, manifests, and radio traffic — not theft.

fixed_truth.motive: Avoid commission discipline and negligence findings after Henry died during unauthorized lens repair Tom had warned against
fixed_truth.method: Discovered Henry's body after a gallery fall, then falsified voluntary-departure entries in the log book and radio traffic
fixed_truth.opportunity: Acting keeper on watch; access to log book, radio terminal, and supply tally signatures

Henry Walsh fell from the gallery safety railing during lens repair

Landing operations were closed from 0345 to 0715 due to squall conditions
Pilot Frank Morales flew no passenger off the station during the night
Henry Walsh's personal trunk TRK-HENRY-014 never scanned outbound
Gallery railing shows fresh scrape marks and a bent rail pin at the lens access point
Lens toolkit LSK-7 was checked out to Henry for scheduled service two days earlier
Relief keeper Sarah Chen was not told the true status of Henry Walsh before arrival

Weather chart CLOSED status contradicts any claimed 0430 voluntary boat or rotor departure

dialogue.scene: Sarah checks the duty roster on her clipboard.
dialogue.speaker: Sarah Chen
dialogue.quote: Henry was supposed to hand over at 0600. Tom radioed that Henry chose to leave early on my inbound hop window, but I never spoke to Henry myself.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Sarah speaks quietly, glancing toward the gallery stairs.
dialogue.speaker: Sarah Chen
dialogue.quote: The gallery lamp was running, but Henry's bunk was already stripped and his seabag was gone from the locker room. That felt wrong for a man who lived for his routines.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Sarah taps the copied radio summary sheet.
dialogue.speaker: Sarah Chen
dialogue.quote: Tom's 0410 weather log says Henry departed voluntary at 0430. I copied that into my relief report because it was the only narrative on record.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Frank spreads the flight clipboard on a cargo crate.
dialogue.speaker: Frank Morales
dialogue.quote: I did not fly a passenger off this rock last night. My manifest shows only inbound diesel and mail pouches.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Frank points at the annotated weather strip.
dialogue.speaker: Frank Morales
dialogue.quote: Squall line closed the landing from 0345 until 0715. Nobody was taking a voluntary boat or rotor off in that window.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Frank highlights a line on the cargo list.
dialogue.speaker: Frank Morales
dialogue.quote: Henry's marked personal trunk is still listed on my inbound manifest as awaiting outbound load. If he left, he did it without his gear.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Maya pulls the supply manifest binder open.
dialogue.speaker: Maya Ortiz
dialogue.quote: Trunk tag TRK-HENRY-014 is still in the landing inventory. It never scanned outbound.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Maya traces the signature column with her pencil.
dialogue.speaker: Maya Ortiz
dialogue.quote: Tom signed the 0430 departure tally as acting keeper. Henry's signature is absent from every outbound line.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.speaker: Maya Ortiz
dialogue.quote: Lens shim kit LSK-7 was checked out to Henry two days ago for scheduled service, not emergency repair.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Tom keeps his eyes on the log book.
dialogue.speaker: Tom Reed
dialogue.quote: Henry got restless after the storm forecast. He said he would catch the early window and left me to finish the watch.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Tom's voice tightens when he mentions the gallery.
dialogue.speaker: Tom Reed
dialogue.quote: Henry insisted on calibrating the Fresnel segments alone. I told him the gallery rail was slick after the salt spray, but he went up anyway.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.

dialogue.scene: Tom closes the log book with deliberate care.
dialogue.speaker: Tom Reed
dialogue.quote: I logged his voluntary departure at 0430 so the commission would not panic before relief arrived. That is standard when a keeper abandons post.
dialogue.coda: You note the answer in your case file.
